summary: Eitri and Sindri may name the same smith in different textual/reference traditions, but automatic merging would erase witness differences.
resolution_notes: Collect manuscript readings and edition apparatus before resolution.

summary: Hesiod’s Theogony narrates Aphrodite arising from the aftermath of Uranus’s castration, while the Iliad names Dione as her mother and elsewhere calls Aphrodite a daughter of Zeus.
resolution_notes: Retain the Hesiodic and Iliadic witnesses as coexisting source-level variants; do not force a single normalized parentage.

summary: Greek sources preserve more than one figure named Perses; the Hesiodic parent of Hecate must not be automatically merged with homonymous figures.
resolution_notes: Create witness-specific candidates and compare parentage, generation and narrative role before any identity resolution.

summary: The statuette's lost attribute prevents a secure choice between Zeus and Poseidon.
The Leize thunder spirit in the Classic of Mountains and Seas and later Leigong layers share a thunder function but differ in name, form and textual setting.
resolution_notes: Keep separate canonical entities; future diachronic scholarship may add a qualified relationship without automatic identity.

summary: Raijin can function as a broad thunder-kami designation while classical and regional traditions preserve multiple distinct thunder figures.
resolution_notes: Use an umbrella entity plus separate deity/group records; never force a single universal genealogy.

summary: Modern thunder-god labels can obscure that Takemikazuchi’s principal classical actions are martial and emissarial.
resolution_notes: Retain martial/heavenly-envoy as primary and thunder association as medium-confidence secondary classification.

summary: Old Norse witnesses make Hel a child of Loki and do not make Loki Thor’s brother; Marvel screen continuity makes Loki an adoptive brother and Hela a half-sister of Thor.
resolution_notes: Keep ancient and modern entities separate and connect them only through modern_adaptations.

summary: Modern summaries often give Perun a named axe or hammer, but the registered medieval chronicle evidence does not name such a unique divine weapon.
resolution_notes: Add archaeological miniature-axe pendants and comparative scholarship only as low-confidence, separately sourced layers.

summary: Baal can be a lord/master title while the Ugaritic Baalu/Haddu dossier refers to a particular storm-deity figure in registered witnesses.
resolution_notes: Never merge Baal Hammon, Baalshamin, Melqart, biblical Baalim or other regional figures by name alone.
